summary: Peeks the two end values currently held in the queue stored at this+0x0 via QueuePeek and returns their difference (second peeked value minus first), yielding the scalar range width the queue contents span. The caller set (TelemetryDisplaySwitch plus a thunk to this function) is consistent with a display helper that turns queued samples into a single width value.

local_names.v1: queue object pointer read from this+0x0

operations.description: Dereference the queue pointer v1 from this+0x0.
Initialize the two peek output floats v4 and v3 to 0.0 before the peek call.
Call QueuePeek(v1, &v4, &v3) to read the two end values currently held in the queue; this is the function's only callee.
Compute the range width as v3 - v4 (second peeked value minus first).
Return the computed difference as the function result.

unresolved: QueuePeek argument order and which end (head/tail) each output represents are not evidenced, so the signed meaning of v3 - v4 is a DERIVED label.
The element type and units of the queued values, and therefore the physical meaning of the returned width, are unknown; the TelemetryDisplaySwitch caller suggests a telemetry range widget.
